minutes.headline: Design committee reviewed revised Town Hall/Ritter plans with a PAC basement; only vote was adjournment, cost estimates due Feb 3.
minutes.summary: Taylor and Burns presented updated site, floor and exterior plans for a new Town Hall, a Ritter renovation for school offices and an Old Town Hall meeting house. The PAC studio moved into a 12-foot-deep basement under the new Town Hall. Members and the public commented on basement and ledge cost risk, slope walkway safety, and school/town co-location; an update on mothballing a building with asbestos was given, and the meeting adjourned by roll call as quorum was about to be lost.

public_comment.topic: Plan looks not cost effective; digging 12 feet; favors renovating existing buildings, separating school and town between Ritter and Town Hall, possibly expanding into the Town Hall attic.
Asked about PAC studio square footage, secure late access, ceiling height, floor, and HVAC humidity control.
Questions on school security, ACE access, reception, parking and public/student mixing in Ritter.

votes.motion: Move to adjourn (roll call: Roy, Gray, Allison, Scull and Briny, chair all aye)

budget_items.topic: PAC studio in basement vs freestanding building
budget_items.what_was_said: Architect said putting the PAC in a basement under the new Town Hall saves considerable cost compared with a separate building.
A member worried ledge or groundwater could make the deep basement costly; no borings have been done.
Chair said the program shrank from the starting square footage to a smaller figure.
Cost estimating is under way, with estimates expected at the Feb 3 meeting.

budget_items.topic: Earlier renovation estimate of the other building
budget_items.what_was_said: Chair recalled the earlier renovation price tag, about half of it code upgrades, led to the community shifting direction.

decisions.decision: Chair will send the architects' presentation to staff for feedback and return it to the team by end of the week; architects to add black-and-white furnishing plans and room square footages by the next day.
Cost estimates expected at the Feb 3 remote meeting; joint meeting with the Select Board Feb 4.
Rescheduling of the Feb 17 meeting (Presidents Day) deferred to Feb 3.

what_happened.line: The Municipal Building Design Committee took no votes on the plans; its only vote was a roll-call adjournment as quorum was about to be lost.
Architects presented revised plans for a new Town Hall, a Ritter renovation for school offices and an Old Town Hall meeting house, with the PAC studio moved into a basement.
A member raised the risk that ledge or groundwater could raise the cost of the deep basement; no borings have been done.
Cost estimates are expected at the Feb 3 remote meeting, with a joint meeting with the Select Board on Feb 4.
A resident said the plan looks not cost effective and favored renovating existing buildings; a rescheduling of the Feb 17 meeting was deferred to Feb 3.

why_it_matters: The committee is shaping a town building project whose cost has not yet been estimated, so any figure a resident is later asked to approve will rest on the Feb 3 estimates and on soil conditions not yet tested.
The basement design for the PAC studio is presented as a cost saving over a separate building, but that saving has not been checked against ledge or groundwater, because no borings exist.
